title: Extracellular Enzyme Assays for NAG, BG, and CBH
author: Mia Maltz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jg3cjyn
materials: The slope is your Extinction Coefficient (ε ).

steps.title: Weigh soil sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 1–2 g wet soil, record the exact mass, and place the soil into a labeled 500 mL container.

steps.title: Prepare homogenate slurry
steps.instruction: Add 125 mL acetate buffer to the container, blend on the highest speed for 1 minute to obtain a homogenate slurry. Rinse the blender with de‑ionized water between samples.

steps.title: Dispense homogenate to assay plate
steps.instruction: Using a multi‑channel pipette equipped with wide‑mouth tips trimmed with scissors, add homogenate to each designated well so that each well contains a total volume of 250 µL.

steps.title: Incubate assay plate
steps.instruction: Place the plate in an incubator set to the appropriate soil temperature (e.g., 10 °C for Alaskan soils) and incubate for 1 hour.

steps.title: Add alkaline stop solution
steps.instruction: Immediately after the 1‑hour incubation, add 10 µL of 1 M NaOH to each well, record the addition time, and allow the plate to sit for 10 minutes to let NaOH react with MUB.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Read the plate on a fluorescence plate reader using 365 nm excitation and 450 nm emission.

steps.title: Generate MUB standard curves
steps.instruction: For the soil‑containing plate, calculate the homogenate blank by averaging the fluorescence values in column 11. Then, for each MUB concentration, average the replicate wells, subtract the homogenate blank, and plot fluorescence versus MUB concentration (μmol L⁻¹) to obtain a linear regression slope. In a separate plate containing only buffer (no homogenate), repeat the same procedure to create an unquenched standard curve; this provides the true MUB fluorescence and the quench coefficient.

substeps.instruction: Average fluorescence for each MUB concentration.
Subtract homogenate blank from each averaged value.
Perform linear regression (MUB concentration on x‑axis, fluorescence on y‑axis) to obtain slope.
Repeat steps a–d on a buffer‑only plate to obtain the unquenched slope.

steps.title: Calculate enzyme activity
steps.instruction:
Compute the quench coefficient as (Quench control – Homogenate control) / Standard Fluorescence. Determine net fluorescence units (NFU) = [(Assay – Homogenate control) / Quench coefficient] – Substrate control. Finally, calculate activity (nmol h⁻¹ g⁻¹) using:

Activity = (NFU × Buffer vol (mL)) / (ε × Homogenate vol (mL) × Time (h) × Soil mass (g))

where Assay volume = 0.250 mL, Homogenate volume = 0.200 mL, Buffer volume ≈ 125 mL (the volume used to dilute the soil), and Soil mass is the mass recorded in step 1 (wet, dry, organic matter, or Cmic as desired).
